parameters.query:
-- Which candidate shops can actually serve this order?
-- PLU lives in raw_ls_products.sku (there is no plu column) and push_lightspeed_order only
-- accepts rows with visible = true and a non-empty sku, so this mirrors its Load LS Catalog
-- SKUs node exactly. Modifier PLUs count too: the pusher validates those as well.
-- deliverect_active is NOT limited to takeaway: the live IF NOT Deliverect Active? node has
-- exactly one condition, on deliverect_active, and every order pulled off the queue passes
-- through it. A Shopify order offered to a deliverect shop would be yielded there too.
WITH bestelling AS (
  SELECT co.items
    FROM public.canonical_orders co
   WHERE co.id = $1::uuid
), regel AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT plu FROM (
    SELECT jsonb_array_elements(b.items)->>'plu' AS plu FROM bestelling b
    UNION ALL
    SELECT jsonb_array_elements(jsonb_array_elements(b.items)->'modifiers')->>'plu' FROM bestelling b
  ) s
   WHERE plu IS NOT NULL AND plu <> ''
), kandidaat AS (
  SELECT value AS location_key FROM jsonb_array_elements_text($2::jsonb) AS t(value)
)
SELECT k.location_key,
       (dl.location_key IS NOT NULL)                                        AS bestaat,
       COALESCE(dl.is_active, true)                                         AS actief,
       COALESCE(dl.deliverect_active, false)                                AS deliverect_slikt,
       m.ontbrekende_plus,
       (dl.location_key IS NOT NULL
        AND COALESCE(dl.is_active, true)
        AND NOT COALESCE(dl.deliverect_active, false)
        AND cardinality(m.ontbrekende_plus) = 0)                            AS aanbiedbaar
  FROM kandidaat k
  CROSS JOIN bestelling b
  LEFT JOIN public.dim_location dl ON dl.location_key = k.location_key
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT ARRAY(
      SELECT r.plu FROM regel r
       WHERE NOT EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM public.raw_ls_products p
          WHERE p.location_key = k.location_key
            AND p.sku = r.plu
            AND p.visible = true)
    ) AS ontbrekende_plus
  ) m
 ORDER BY k.location_key;

-- Cancel at the origin shop, recreate at the target, and queue the push:
-- ONE statement, ONE transaction. Either all three happen or none of them does. An earlier
-- draft transitioned and enqueued in a second node; a failure between the two left the origin
-- cancelled and the new row sitting at 'received' with nothing watching it.
-- location_key is immutable by design (both normalizers exclude it from DO UPDATE SET), and
-- Lightspeed has no cancel/update call, so a new row is the only way to make the target till
-- print. $1 = canonical_id, $2 = target location_key.
WITH oud_status AS (
  -- Same snapshot as the UPDATE below, so this is the status BEFORE the cancel.
  SELECT status, shipday_order_id FROM public.canonical_orders WHERE id = $1::uuid
), oud AS (
  UPDATE public.canonical_orders
     SET status = 'cancelled'::public.order_state,
         cancel_reason = 'overname_naar_' || $2::text,
         updated_at = now()
   WHERE id = $1::uuid
     -- is_allowed_order_state_transition() on prod refuses complete -> cancelled and
     -- ls_rejected -> cancelled (and cancelled -> cancelled). Naming the legal set here
     -- turns a trigger exception into an empty result the Guard node reports honestly.
     AND status IN ('received', 'normalized', 'pushing_ls', 'ls_sent',
                    'ls_accepted', 'shipday_sent', 'ls_failed')
  RETURNING *
), nieuw AS (
  INSERT INTO public.canonical_orders (
    schema_version, source, external_ref, location_key, order_type, status,
    customer, items, payment, vat_lines, utm, raw_payload_id, correlation_id
  )
  SELECT o.schema_version, o.source,
         -- MUST differ: ON CONFLICT (source, external_ref) is the arbiter both normalizers
         -- use, and external_ref is also the Lightspeed idempotency key (externalReference),
         -- which push_lightspeed_order compares in Filter LS Idempotency. The name of the
         -- origin shop is read from dim_location, never taken from the caller: it rides onto
         -- the printed ticket through Build Order Payload.
         -- LEFT JOIN + COALESCE, like Load Canonical Order in push_lightspeed_order: an inner
         -- join here would cancel the origin, insert nothing, return no rows and still COMMIT
         -- if the origin's shop were missing from dim_location.
         o.external_ref || ' · OVERNAME ' || upper(COALESCE(dlo.name, o.location_key)),
         $2::text, o.order_type,
         -- Straight to 'normalized' on purpose: push_lightspeed_order's State -> pushing_ls
         -- only picks up 'normalized' or 'ls_failed', and nothing watches 'received'.
         -- Step 0 of the runbook checks that no INSERT trigger forces 'received' here.
         'normalized'::public.order_state,
         o.customer, o.items, o.payment, o.vat_lines, o.utm, o.raw_payload_id,
         gen_random_uuid()
    FROM oud o
    LEFT JOIN public.dim_location dlo ON dlo.location_key = o.location_key
  RETURNING id, source, external_ref, location_key
)
-- The courier is NOT moved here. If the origin order already has a Shipday ride, a person
-- deletes it at the origin shop and creates it again at the target; see "Deliberately not
-- automated" in docs/migrations/2026-09-10-overname-door.md. oud_shipday_order_id is returned
-- so the OS knows whether it must nag about that at all.
SELECT true                                        AS ok,
       n.id                                        AS canonical_id,
       n.external_ref,
       (SELECT location_key FROM oud)              AS van_location_key,
       (SELECT status FROM oud_status)             AS oude_status,
       (SELECT shipday_order_id FROM oud_status)   AS oud_shipday_order_id,
       public.pgmq_send_order('q_orders_push_ls', jsonb_build_object(
         'canonical_id', n.id,
         'source',       n.source,
         'external_ref', n.external_ref,
         'location_key', n.location_key,
         'origin',       'overname'))              AS msg_id
  FROM nieuw n;
